turns.prompt_text: I have a fish tank and I'm wondering what it is sealed with
turns.response_html:
Most modern glass aquariums are sealed with high-strength RTV silicone. This specialized 100% silicone adhesive remains flexible while providing a waterproof, chemical-resistant bond that can withstand the constant hydrostatic pressure of the water.

Older tanks or custom builds might use:

  • Epoxy resins: Common in plywood or large acrylic-to-glass transitions.
  • Glazing putty: Found in antique metal-framed tanks (though these are often resealed with silicone today).
  • Solvent welding: Used for acrylic tanks, where a chemical agent like Weld-On actually melts the plastic pieces into a single solid unit.
